correctness.rationale: The object is the one-sided word with marks at B^j (j>=0), not at zero. Unique factorization of B^b-B^a=B^a(B^(b-a)-1) by the largest dividing power of B, valid for composite bases, proves every possible marked square has one ordered marker pair, hence consecutive B^a,B^(a+1). The predecessor exclusion and s>=0 give exactly the exceptional a=0 starts and x=0..(B-1)B^(a-1)-1 at a>=1. The successor exclusion bounds the maximal periodic extension to 2p+x, establishes least period p, and rules out marked cubes. Counting distinct first-mark offsets, lengths and scales gives M_a, M_a(M_a+1)/2 and cumulative B^m (or B^m+1). Taking the supremum yields the B=2 unattained 5/2 and B>=3 attained 2+1/(B-1) endpoints. Exhaustive independent 624 (base,period) comparisons on B=2..7/p<=104 found precisely the predicted square occurrences; the infinite quantifiers follow from the marker-difference argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The language of marked powers in a canonical automatic sparse word is a motivated combinatorics-on-words object: the ordinary critical exponent is infinite because of zero runs, whereas the marker-qualified exponent and complete nonzero square-root spectrum have a sharp finite base-dependent description. The full all-scale classification, attainable/unattainable boundary and precise counts are mathematical structure, not a one-off small computation.
